identity: Singer and film director · United Kingdom · 1956–2003
title: Leslie Cheung's birth chart
metaDescription: Leslie Cheung's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 19.3° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mutable signs carry four of the ten placements whose signs are settled — the broadest certain weighting in the chart. The mutable signs sit where one season is already becoming the next — the scheme’s translators.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 19.3° Virgo — the second decan, 10°–20°, which the tradition sub-rules by Saturn. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Virgo and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 12.1° Libra, Venus was at 3.8° Leo, Mars was at 17.8° Pisces. Read together: a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Neptune and Pluto hold the closest angle here — a sextile, 0.3° wide. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Saturn square Pluto at 1.4°, and the Sun opposition Mars at 1.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Mercury stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has one entry for this chart. Jupiter in Virgo at 13.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives fire 4, earth 2, air 2, water 2, and mutable 4, fixed 4, cardinal 2 across the modes. Fire weights a chart toward initiative — starting, asserting, spending energy to find out what happens. Mars was retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Sagittarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.1° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 20.6°.
